$comment: Provenance for the lesser GraphQL schema contentus validates its documents against.
WHY A PINNED COPY AND NOT INTROSPECTION. A client that asks the instance what its
schema is can only ever discover that it agreed with whatever it was pointed at.
The question this repository needs answered at BUILD time is different: do the
documents contentus sends match the contract lesser publishes? That contract is a
file in the lesser repository at a known ref, so it is pinned here by digest and
the answer is deterministic, offline, and identical on every machine.
WHAT THE DIGEST IS FOR. Not tamper-proofing — an author who edits the schema can
edit the digest in the same commit. It is for making that edit VISIBLE: moving the
pin is a change to contracts/, in the diff, with a ref to check it against, rather
than a silent edit to a large SDL file nobody re-reads. The control it composes
with is cross-client adversarial review, not this field alone.
MOVING THE PIN. Copy the file from lesser at the new ref, update `ref`, `sha256`
and `bytes` together, and run `pnpm run validate:graphql`. Every document is
re-validated against the new schema, so a field lesser removed fails the build in
the same commit that adopts the removal — which is the entire point of pinning it
rather than trusting it.
This file is READ BY A GATE. `gov-infra/verifiers/strict-json.mjs` semantics apply:
a duplicate key is a value the reviewer reads and a different value the control
enforces, so duplicates are rejected rather than last-wins.
The canonical schema is one self-contained SDL document: `type Query` plus the
`extend type Query` blocks that carry the CMS, messaging, agent and drone
surfaces. graphql-js merges extensions when building, so the CMS fields
contentus reads (`articles`, `articleBySlug`, `draftPreview`, `myDrafts`,
`sharedDraftReviews`) resolve from the same build as the core schema.
Where the gate looks for documents. `src` is walked whole — every TypeScript
module AND every Svelte component, because a component's <script> can declare
and send a document exactly as a module can, and a walk keyed on `.ts` would
have been a file-set assumption dressed up as coverage.
Vendored greater-components source, managed by the `greater` CLI and never
hand-edited. Its adapter layer carries GraphQL documents written against
GREATER's own projection of a fediverse server — `Account`, `Post`, `Status` —
and lesser's schema has no such types at all (`type Account` does not exist;
the equivalent is `type Actor`). Validating them against lesser's contract
does not report a contract defect, it reports that they answer a different
contract.
THIS IS A DISCLOSURE, NOT A PERMISSION. The counts below are asserted exactly:
a vendored document appearing, disappearing, or changing shape fails the gate
and has to be re-declared deliberately. And the reason the exclusion is SAFE is
checked rather than asserted — `boundary` below is the control, and
tests/graphql-contract.test.mjs re-proves it against the real build, where a
module that is loaded is a module that can execute.
upstream_trees.reason: greater-components adapter documents target greater's own schema (Account/Post/Status), which lesser does not define; contentus does not import or execute them
upstream_trees.boundary: no module outside this tree may reach a document-bearing module inside it
